task.description:
Hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER's design at lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md. Re-derive your verdict independently -- do not accept CODE-DESIGNER's own result.summary claims at face value (core-directives.md: 'a validator that only reads the producer's result.summary and says PASS has not validated anything').

Specifically re-check, by reading the actual files yourself:

1. Read test/letflow/secrets_test.exs and test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs YOURSELF in full. Independently verify, against ISS-0113's three named failure mechanisms, that neither file (a) calls Sandbox.checkout/1 itself, (b) spawns a second process doing concurrent real Postgres work, or (c) calls provision_tenant_schema!/replay_migrations!/provisioned_tenant! a second time within any test body. If you find ANY of these in either file, this is a BLOCKER -- CODE-DESIGNER's own classification was wrong and cannot ship.
2. Read test/letflow/service_catalog_test.exs and test/letflow/routers/onboarding_test.exs yourself and confirm they are genuinely correctly EXCLUDED (i.e. confirm the Task.start/async row-lock claim for service_catalog_test.exs, and confirm onboarding_test.exs's own ad-hoc Sandbox.mode(:auto) call is real and out of this design's TenantFixture-scoped procedure).
3. Re-derive the peak-concurrent-DBConnection-checkout arithmetic in design section 5 yourself -- confirm System.schedulers_online() is genuinely uncapped by any --max-cases override anywhere in this repo (grep test_helper.exs, mix.exs, config/test.exs, .github/workflows/ci.yml yourself), and confirm the pool_size figures (32 for plain mix test, 5 for a test_parallel.sh partition at N=16) are correct against config/test.exs and decision 0009's own formula, not merely copied from CODE-DESIGNER's summary.
4. Confirm the opt-in mechanism (opts[:restore_sandbox], default false) as designed does NOT change behavior for any of the other 44 TenantFixture call sites -- re-read test/support/tenant_fixture.ex's current provisioned_tenant!/1 and confirm the design's described insertion point (after existing step 6, before return) and its on_exit/LIFO-ordering claim (new restore-to-:auto callback must run AFTER the existing schema-drop teardown, which was registered earlier -- confirm ExUnit's on_exit really is LIFO, this is a genuinely checkable factual claim, not just design prose).
5. Confirm zero implementation code is present in the design doc (design artefacts carry signatures/@specs only).
6. Confirm the design explicitly reconciles against decision 0009/ISS-0287 rather than merely asserting consistency.

Gate PASS only if every one of ISS-0423's original 6 acceptance criteria (task queue's own AC1-AC6, restated in your handoff's acceptance_criteria below) has a concrete design element you can point to, and if your own independent file reads in steps 1-2 above confirm CODE-DESIGNER's classification rather than merely trusting it.
acceptance_criteria: Independently confirmed (own file read) that secrets_test.exs and webhooks_test.exs hit none of ISS-0113's three failure mechanisms
Independently confirmed that service_catalog_test.exs and onboarding_test.exs are correctly excluded, with the specific evidence (line/construct) cited
Independently re-derived (not copied) the peak-concurrent-checkout numbers and pool_size figures against real config/decision-0009 text
Confirmed the on_exit/LIFO ordering claim is factually correct for ExUnit
Confirmed zero implementation code appears in the design artefact
Confirmed decision 0009/ISS-0287 is explicitly and correctly reconciled
PASS or FAIL verdict stated with specific evidence per point, not a general impression
